items.title: Meta Withdraws $25 Million from Its Midterms Push
items.author: Theodore Schleifer
items.content: <article>The company outlined a $65 million budget last year when it embarked on an effort to elect state politicians friendly to the A.I. industry.</article>

items.title: Why No One Can Look Away From Elizabeth Holmes
items.author: Max Read, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Chris Wood, Dan Powell, Rowan Niemisto and Diane Wong
items.content: <article>“I felt like there were some moments in the film where she was just brazenly lying.”</article>

items.title: Tesla Debuts 2026 Roadster ‘Flying’ Electric Sports Car
items.author: Jack Ewing
items.content: <article>Elon Musk’s company and other automakers, like Jaguar and Bentley, are trying to sell very expensive electric cars to people who usually prefer gasoline-fueled luxury and performance.</article>

items.title: Ms., Martians and Guacamole: Their First Time in The Times
items.author: The New York Times and Joanna Ni
items.content: <article>Our reporters share a compendium of debuts, discoveries and (sometimes overdue) appearances in the paper.</article>

items.title: OpenAI Engineer, Who Is Charged With Planting Bug, Advised Saudis
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>The employee, now fired, had said he advised government agencies in Saudi Arabia. He was also listed as a partner at a venture firm with a Saudi prince.</article>

items.title: Exhausted Parents Are Turning to A.I. Apps Despite the Risks
items.author: Alisha Haridasani Gupta and Katie Van Syckle
items.content: <article>Even as alarm grows over the risks, families are embracing bots and agents to tackle the spiraling administrative tasks of modern child rearing.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Says Revenue Jumped 45% to $16.8 Billion in Third Quarter
items.author: Lauren Hirsch and Sri Muppidi
items.content: <article>The company held an investor meeting on Wednesday as it plans a blockbuster initial public offering as soon as next month.</article>

items.title: Senators Question Meta’s Data Center Tax Strategy
items.author: Kashmir Hill
items.content: <article>Democrats on the Senate Finance Committee sent a letter to Mark Zuckerberg, Meta’s chief executive, questioning the company’s $6.6 billion in tax breaks.</article>

items.title: 22 People Got Together For a Dinner Party. So Did Their A.I. Agents.
items.author: Erin Griffith
items.content: <article>As artificial intelligence bots spread, we are increasingly glimpsing how these digital entities interact and what they talk about with one another.</article>

items.title: Netflix, Facing Slowing Growth, Cuts 6% of Its Work Force
items.author: John Koblin
items.content: <article>The streamer’s share price is down more than 40 percent over the last year as the company has struggled with stalling engagement.</article>

items.title: Rogue A.I. Agents from China Chatted with Researchers
items.author: Dylan Freedman
items.content: <article>Researchers discovered that the agents were trying to bypass security controls on websites and made contact with them. A Times reporter was invited to join the discussion.</article>

items.title: F.B.I. Arrests OpenAI Employee Accused of Planting Bug in Office
items.author: Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>OpenAI said that the employee had placed a device built to evade detection and that he had planned to secretly record meetings in other sensitive spaces.</article>

items.title: NASA’s Perseverance Rover Sets a Mars Driving Record
items.author: Kenneth Chang
items.content: <article>Advances in self-driving technology have made it easier to traverse distant worlds.</article>

items.title: Apple Introduces HomeView, a $299 Tablet for the Home
items.author: Kalley Huang and Emmy Martin
items.content: <article>Apple unveiled the device as it continues its foray into artificial intelligence and tries to prove it can still innovate.</article>

items.title: Is Universal Basic Income the Answer to A.I.-Fueled Job Losses?
items.author: Eli Tan and Rachel Bujalski
items.content: <article>For more than a year, The New York Times followed recipients of universal basic income programs, which Elon Musk and other tech leaders have promoted as a solution to A.I.-fueled job losses.</article>

items.title: Meta Unveils New Series of Advanced A.I. Models
items.author: Eli Tan
items.content: <article>The new models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, are meant to compete with cutting-edge A.I. models from rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI.</article>

items.title: The Times’s New Space Editor Has Her Eye on the Cosmos
items.author: Sarah Bahr
items.content: <article>On the Science desk, Victoria Jaggard spends her days pondering the universe’s most pressing mysteries.</article>

items.title: Three Mark Zuckerbergs, Three Surprisingly Different Men
items.author: Alissa Wilkinson
items.content: <article>Jeremy Strong in “The Social Reckoning,” Jesse Eisenberg in “The Social Network” and the real Meta executive are all playing parts. But only one has changed his approach.</article>

items.title: Justice Dept. Is Investigating TV Networks Over Trump Pool Coverage
items.author: David McCabe, Michael M. Grynbaum, Benjamin Mullin, Lauren Hirsch and Glenn Thrush
items.content: <article>Major TV networks were notified on Friday that the department was examining whether they violated antitrust laws when they suspended pool coverage of President Trump.</article>

items.title: Anthropic Agents Tried to Fill Out Visa Forms on State Dept. Website
items.author: Kate Conger, Mike Isaac, Julian E. Barnes and David E. Sanger
items.content: <article>The Philadelphia Police Department said the agents had also sent in a false homicide tip. The incidents led the White House to call for better disclosure of rogue A.I. behavior.</article>
